title: E7000 Motor/ESC Qualification
revisions: Added production adapter results and the burn-in recommendation

blocks.text: This test qualifies the E7000 motor and ESC combination for use on the AltaX airframe. It answers two questions: whether the combination holds its rated performance across the operating envelope, and where the thermal limit sits under sustained high load.
The deliverable is a burn-in procedure for the arm assemblies, together with the power curve used by the flight-time model.
The unit under test is one complete arm assembly: motor, ESC and propeller adapter, mounted on the bench fixture with the production wiring loom.

blocks.text: Vibration, altitude and salt fog are **not** covered here: they are airframe-level qualifications run under EV1-62, and repeating them at component level would not change the acceptance decision. Propeller balance is also out of scope – the adapter is qualified separately in EV1-41.
Each test drives the ESC from a signal generator through the production loom, with the arm fixed to the bench. The following quantities are logged for every run:

items: Input current and input voltage at the ESC terminals
ESC case temperature, type-K on the FET side

blocks.text: Throttle is expressed as PWM in microseconds throughout, where 1300 µs is idle and 1920 µs is maximum. Runs use one of three stimulus waveforms.

blocks.caption: Stimulus waveforms
rows: Steady-state measurements at every throttle point
Ramp 1300 → 1920 → 1300 µs in 50 µs steps, 5 s dwell per step
Steps between 1150, 1650 and 1950 µs, 10 s dwell
Sustained load at the thermal limit
1850 µs held for 30 min or until failure

blocks.text: Runs start from a cold ESC, defined as case temperature within 3 °C of ambient. A run is discarded if the supply sags below 50.0 V at any point.
Criteria are itemised per test in Table 1 and repeated with the outcome in Table 3. Characterisation and step response are measurements rather than judgements and carry no pass criterion.
All runs used firmware 1.4.2. Raw logs are attached to the test record; the figures below are the reduced data.

P is input power in watts and t is commanded PWM in microseconds, valid from 1300 to 1920 µs at 52.0 V and 23 °C. Peak input power at 1920 µs was 4031 W drawing 77.5 A, at 5180 RPM.

blocks.text: Acceleration from 1150 to 1950 µs settles to within 2 % of the commanded RPM in 410 ms. Deceleration from 1950 to 1150 µs takes 1.28 s, dominated by the propeller inertia rather than the ESC – phase current falls to zero within 40 ms of the command.

An Arduino drove alternating 900 µs and 1300 µs commands to arm and disarm the ESC, with input and phase current logged throughout. The goal was to catch a start-up fault that only appears over many cycles.
The sequence ran 500 cycles with no interruption. Every start-up showed the same current signature, and no cycle showed the synchronisation loss seen on the pre-production adapter.

The first high-load run ended in failure 25 s into the 1850 µs hold. Input current collapsed from 71 A to zero within one log sample and the motor stopped; ESC case temperature at the last good sample was 106 °C.

The ESC used in that run was a bare board wrapped in heatshrink, with no heatsink and no airflow. Dissection showed at least one failed FET on the phase carrying the highest current, with the surrounding potting discoloured.

Root cause is thermal, not electrical: the part was run outside its cooling configuration. The run was repeated with the production heatsink and 2 m/s of airflow, and completed the full 30 min with the case stabilising at 78 °C. Bare-board operation at sustained high load is therefore excluded, and the burn-in procedure requires the heatsink fitted.

blocks.text: The E7000 motor and ESC combination is qualified for AltaX in the production cooling configuration. It is not qualified for bare-board operation at sustained high load, which failed at 25 s.

items: Release the burn-in procedure in Appendix A of EV1-26-P: 1850 µs for 30 min with the heatsink fitted, case temperature logged, reject above 90 °C.
Use the cubic in section 6.1 for the flight-time model rather than the supplier curve, which overstates power below 1500 µs by up to 9 %.
Temperature extremes remain open and are tracked under EV1-62, owned by the environmental lab. The qualification is conditional on that suite passing.
Repeat arm/disarm cycling once the production adapter reaches revision D – the 500 cycles here used revision C.
